clue.text: Sweet air I must circulate

indicators.note: letters that circulate move around and settle in a different order

parts.note: the three words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone insists on wafting a pleasant breeze around the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone, and a dessert is a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Weedy plant cut

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a broad-leaved weed of fields and verges
second meaning: to reduce or take away, as with wages or a tail

explanation.surface: A gardener lops a straggly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a weak plant being pruned; the two parts are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The common weed with big leaves rubbed on nettle stings shares its name with the verb for docking pay or a tail.

clue.text: Inept Conservative in a huge muddle

indicators.note: one letter sits in the middle of the other jumbled letters
a muddle is a confused mess, so the words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed up
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is caught floundering in a massive mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of 'a huge' split around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche describes someone socially awkward and clumsy, which is close in sense to incompetent or bungling.

clue.text: Spotty headgear capturing one's heart

indicators.note: the headgear captures a letter by holding it inside

parts.note: a bridle is the headgear of a horse

indicators.note: a word's heart is its middle letter

parts.note: the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hat with a pattern of dots has somehow taken someone's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: Headgear suggests a hat, but here it is the harness on a horse's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindle describes an animal's coat that is streaked or flecked with darker patches, so it fits a patchy, speckled appearance.

clue.text: Rex is ideal playing old 23 leader

indicators.note: letters that are playing are moving about freely into a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog called Rex is the perfect companion for an old politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is GOVERNMENT, so the definition means a former head of government: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli was Conservative Prime Minister twice in the nineteenth century, so a past leader of a British administration.

clue.text: Hoodwinked airline's doctor about alcohol left in

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: the doctor's letters wrap about what follows

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine

indicators.note: the side letter goes in the drink word

parts.note: informal word for drink
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A passenger complains that the airline's medic was drinking on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two nestings: the side letter goes into the drink, and the doctor's letters wrap round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bamboozled is to be tricked or deceived, the same idea as being duped or conned.

clue.text: More nasty fellows surrounding a queen

indicators.note: the men are surrounding the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: fellows are men
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant men crowd around a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaner is the comparative of mean in its sense of unkind or spiteful, so nastier.

clue.text: One considered out of date is around after broadcast

indicators.note: after being broadcast, scattered like seed, the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned presenter is still hanging about once the show has aired.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a person a dinosaur is an idiom for someone hopelessly old-fashioned, like the extinct reptiles.

clue.text: Setter's given a long time to make pictures

parts.note: the setter says 'I am', shortened
ages, a very long time

explanation.surface: A puzzle compiler is granted plenty of time to draw something.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the crossword's author, so 'setter's' means 'I am', written I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are visual representations such as drawings or photographs, which plain pictures are.

clue.text: Foul-smelling row of soldiers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: giving off an offensive odour
second meaning: a line of troops standing side by side

explanation.surface: A line of troops gives off a terrible stink.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a stench, and the noun is a single line of troops on parade, as in 'the ranks'.

clue.text: Smuggled pictures returned after trick associated with group

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for pictures is read from its end

parts.note: pictures are works of art
a band is a group

explanation.surface: Stolen paintings are sent back after a scam involving a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' fixes the order: the trick comes first, then the reversed pictures, then the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband means goods brought in illegally, so used adjectivally it describes smuggled items.

clue.text: The end of almost great drink

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: fine, excellent
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Someone is lamenting the last drop of a wonderful beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a show or piece of music, its conclusion.

clue.text: Chief ordered demise of Greek mathematician

parts.note: arch- as in archenemy means chief

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss commanded the death of a mathematician from ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like the boss giving orders, but it is the signal to rearrange 'demise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes of Syracuse was the ancient scholar famous for buoyancy and approximating pi.

clue.text: Load beer clumsily with device for restricting sideways movement at sea

definitions.text: device for restricting sideways movement at sea

indicators.note: doing something clumsily leaves things in a mess and out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Crew sloppily stow beer aboard a sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A leeboard is a board lowered over a boat's side to stop it drifting downwind, acting like a keel.

clue.text: Actors furious about opening in unisex garment

indicators.note: furious suggests wild agitation, throwing the letters into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening in a word is its first letter

parts.note: the initial of the word

explanation.surface: Performers are angry about the start of a gender-neutral costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unisex garment' reads as the definition, but only 'garment' defines; 'unisex' supplies its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcoat is a loose outer robe, historically worn by knights over armour.

clue.text: Tanned suspect going round old island smeared in oil

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the others, enclosing them
something suspect is not quite right, so the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A sunburnt suspect is found on an old island, covered in suntan lotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a person in the surface but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To anoint is to rub or pour oil over someone, often in ceremony, so anointed means greased with it.

clue.text: Drop lecturer with old degree qualification

parts.note: a dip is a drop, as in a road
L is the abbreviation for lecturer
O is the abbreviation for old
MA, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: An academic gives up an outdated postgraduate award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' looks like a verb meaning abandon, but it is the noun for a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a certificate awarded on completing a course of study, an educational credential.

clue.text: Staff do nothing about instrument

parts.note: to man is to staff, as in manning a desk
taken as written

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for zero is read from its end

parts.note: nil is zero

explanation.surface: Employees idle about, doing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like a noun for employees, but it is the verb meaning to provide workers for.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandolin is a stringed musical instrument of the lute family, plucked with a plectrum.

clue.text: One leaving medicine out for native

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of its place, so the letters are rearranged
one is the Roman numeral, and it is leaving, so it is taken away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient walks away from their prescription in favour of a home-grown remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: One I goes from MEDICINE, and the remaining seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic species or disease is one found naturally and only in a particular region, so indigenous to it.

clue.text: Died in home drunkenly clutching top of Jameson bottle

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died
taken as written

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the initial of the whiskey brand

explanation.surface: A drunk passed away at home holding a whiskey bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Jameson is an Irish whiskey; 'in' is part of the anagram letters, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A demijohn is a large, narrow-necked glass or stone vessel used for wine or home brewing.

clue.text: English radical taking overdose crumbled away

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: the radical is taking something in, holding it within

parts.note: a Red is a radical left-winger
OD is short for overdose

explanation.surface: An English revolutionary took too many drugs and fell apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear down gradually, as rock under water or wind, which is to crumble away bit by bit.

clue.text: Nit-picker removing end of chain from necklace

indicators.note: removing means taking something out of the word that follows

parts.note: a pendant is a necklace with a hanging ornament

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fussy jeweller detaches the clasp end of a chain from a necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is someone overly concerned with minor details and rules, a fusser over trivia.

clue.text: Spot a tortoise eating a tuber

indicators.note: the phrase is eating the word, holding it inside itself

parts.note: inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone notices a tortoise munching a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from inside 'Spot' through 'a' into 'tortoise'.
explanation.definitionFit: The potato is the swollen underground stem of its plant, the best-known tuber of all.

clue.text: Domination shown in good bowling spell by new chaps at last

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
in cricket an over is a spell of six balls
N is the abbreviation for new
chaps are men

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the little word

explanation.surface: A cricket team's supremacy comes from a fine spell by fresh bowlers at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled in a row. 'At last' reads as finally, but means the last letter of 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Government is the exercise of authority and control over a people, so rule or domination.

clue.text: Mist envelopes rare creature

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap round, so the mist holds a letter inside

parts.note: fog is thick mist
R is the abbreviation for rare

explanation.surface: A haze shrouds an elusive animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog is an amphibian, an animal, so it is an example of a living being.

clue.text: Touch female fish

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: Someone handles a fish of the female sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel something is to explore it with the hands, the sense of contact.

clue.text: Serious cut close to ankle

parts.note: to sever is to cut off

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A grave wound has been inflicted near someone's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as near, but means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe injury or problem is grave and acute, matching the sense of grave or critical.

clue.text: Greatly daring, I printed translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into a different form, so the letters are rendered anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bold publisher boasts of having issued a foreign version of a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid describes someone fearless and adventurous, bold in facing danger.
